chunks: 5204 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who intentionally killed a Muslim man, and the slain man had no heirs among the Muslims except relatives from the Ahl al-Dhimmah from among his kin.

He عليه السلام said: “It is upon the Imam to present Islam to his relatives from the people of his household. Whoever among them accepts Islam, then he is his heir, and the killer is handed over to him. If he wishes, he may kill; if he wishes, he may pardon; and if he wishes, he may take the blood money. But if none of his relatives accepts Islam, then the Imam is the authority over his affair. If he wishes, he may kill; and if he wishes, he may take the blood money and place it in the Bayt al-Mal of the Muslims, because the liability concerning the slain man was upon the Imam, and likewise his blood money belongs to the Imam of the Muslims.”
I said: “Then if the Imam pardons him?” He عليه السلام said: “It is only a right belonging to all the Muslims. The Imam is only to kill or to take the blood money, and he has no right to pardon.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: Non-Muslim protected subjects living under Islamic rule.
key_terms.إِمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The Imam as the governing authority over the Muslim community.
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: Blood money paid as legal compensation for killing.
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The public treasury of the Muslims.
key_terms.جِنَايَةَ الْمَقْتُولِ: The legal liability or protected claim arising from the slain person’s killing.
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: The legal heir or authorized claimant over the slain person’s case.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a murdered Muslim has no Muslim heirs and only non-Muslim relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding intentional killing when the slain Muslim has no Muslim heirs, but only non-Muslim relatives from the Ahl al-Dhimmah. It states that the Imam must first offer Islam to those relatives, and if none accepts, the Imam assumes authority over the case and may pursue qisas or take the diyyah for the Bayt al-Mal, but may not pardon because the right belongs to the Muslim community.
